checks.detail: the retry hit no dead end
all audited paths inside the sandbox

cases.why:
THE MEASUREMENT FOR ITEM 6. `notes` is a DIRECTORY, so run 1 drafts read_file on it, the step dead-ends ('is a directory - use list_directory instead'), and the replan loop routes around it. Run 2 asks the IDENTICAL goal against the SAME sandbox and the SAME database, so what run 1 recorded is available to the planner. Rule 23's own worked example is exactly this case.

TWO NUMBERS, NOT ONE. `retry_signal_present` asks whether the mechanism ENGAGED (was the record there and readable?); `retry_no_repeat_failure` asks whether it CHANGED ANYTHING. Conflating those is how the 2026-07-17 fan-out shipped a feature that never fired while 1,578 tests stayed green.

*** THIS CASE'S FIRST RUN FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS, BOTH MINE, AND BOTH ARE WHY IT IS WRITTEN THE WAY IT IS. ***
(1) Run 1 COMPLETED - the planner recovered on its own - so a failure_intelligence that filtered on `status == failed` saw NOTHING, and run 2 walked into the same wall and paid another ~24s replan. A dead end is not the same thing as a failed plan, and the recovered kind is the common one. The query now reads failed STEPS as well as failed plans (see STEP_RECOVERED).
(2) The expectation was `retry_avoids_tools: [read_file]`, which is UNANSWERABLE for a tool the goal legitimately needs: read_file on the DIRECTORY is the dead end, read_file on the file inside it is the answer. A bench that asserts the wrong thing manufactures defects - the same lesson `ghost-file` records. It now pins the narrow, checkable claim: the retry did not walk into a failed step at all.

*** THE SECOND NUMBER IS STILL ALLOWED TO BE ZERO. *** If it is, the recorded instruction is NOT to rewrite the prompt - this codebase has measured prompt-only rules at zero three separate times. Either find a comparator or delete the block. See the honest limit in app/core/failure_intelligence.py.
